1B.4.note: Partially met, and the remaining gap is Go-only. KOTLIN CORRECTION (2026-07-27): this entry previously claimed Kotlin emits optional non-array SCALARS with zero-value sentinels (Boolean = false, Int = 0, Long = 0L). That has been FALSE since #424 — zero such defaults exist in the generated Kotlin models. Kotlin also distinguishes the third wire state, required-and-nullable, as `T?` with NO default (vs `T? = null` for optional), so an omitted key still fails to decode. Both halves are pinned by check-kotlin-optional-arrays-and-scalars, which covers arrays and primitive scalars on models and on request bodies resolved via each operation's requestBody reference (object/$ref/enum members stay out of scope — reference types with no sentinel to guard). REMAINING GAP (why pass stays false) — this is a STATIC-TYPE violation in Go, not merely a runtime one. Go optional non-pointer scalars cannot represent absence in the type at all: e.g. optional UpdateCardColumnRequestContent.Description is generated as `string` with `omitempty`, so absence and an explicit "" are indistinguishable on the wire AND the empty string is unsendable. That is exactly what SPEC.md §10 Optional Fields forbids, and it applies to request shapes (where it silently drops a caller's intent) as well as response shapes (where decode collapses absence into the zero value). Ruby/Swift have a separate, narrower runtime issue: they decode faithfully but drop nil on RE-ENCODE (compact / synthesized encoder). Remediation is per-schema via the existing x-go-type-skip-optional-pointer precedent — set `false` on a field to force a pointer and restore the distinction; the global prefer-skip-optional-pointer: true default is what produces the collapse. It must NOT be resolved by treating the width/height carve-out as a blanket omitempty waiver, since that carve-out is response-only. Documented in SPEC.md §10 and tracked in #436. Go's *[]T is used only where rich-text projections need the wire distinction round-tripped both directions; not a blanket sweep.
